text: A terminal workspace for Windows, made for working with AI coding agents such as Claude Code. vyberun keeps your projects, terminals and servers in one window. Each project and server is a card in the sidebar, and each card has its own terminal tabs. Click a card and its tabs are there as you left them, still running, even after vyberun was closed. A space for one ticket, with its projects as cards and a Claude Code tab on the right.

head: What it does
text: Tabs that keep running. Tabs don't stop when vyberun closes. They come back with their output when you open it again. See Sessions that survive . Spaces and cards. Group projects, terminals and servers into spaces, for example one space per ticket. Each card keeps its own tabs. Any shell. Git Bash, PowerShell, Command Prompt or Ubuntu (WSL), chosen per tab, with split panes. Servers. Connect over SSH with a key, a password or a saved PuTTY session. Work can keep running on the server after you disconnect. Nothing is installed on the server. AI agents that work as a team. Give each Claude Code tab a role, such as backend, frontend or QA. Agents know their teammates, hand work to each other, and can read other tabs when you allow it. Status at a glance. Each tab shows whether its agent is working, waiting for you or finished, and each space sums up what runs in it. Search everything. Search files and folders on your PC, your tabs, cards and settings, and inside Claude Code conversations. Screenshots. Capture a selection or a whole long conversation as one picture, mark it up and share it.

head: Who it's for
text: vyberun is for developers on Windows who work in terminals all day, often with more than one project, server or agent at a time. You don't need Claude Code to use it: everything except the agent features works with any shell and any command-line program.

head: What it isn't
text: It isn't a code editor. Open a project in your editor from its card. It doesn't need an account or a sign-in, and it doesn't send your data anywhere. It doesn't install anything on your servers or change their settings.

head: Requirements
text: Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) or Windows 11, 64-bit. Optional: Git for Windows for Git Bash tabs, WSL for Ubuntu tabs, PuTTY for saved PuTTY sessions and .ppk keys, Claude Code for the agent features. vyberun is in alpha: it's used every day, but things can still change between versions. Next: Installing .

Get vyberun from the Microsoft Store, or use the zip. There are two ways to get vyberun. They're the same program. Microsoft Store Zip .NET Included Install the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime once Updates Automatic Unzip the new version over the old one Signed Yes, by Microsoft No: Windows may warn you the first time Where it runs from Installed by Windows Any folder you choose

head: From the Microsoft Store
kw: ms store install get winget command line
text: Open vyberun in the Microsoft Store and choose Get . Start vyberun from the Start menu. You can also install it from a terminal: winget install vyberun This installs the same Store version, signed by Microsoft. winget install 9MX9G62RFFQ5 (its Store ID) does the same.

head: From the zip
kw: smartscreen smart app control unsigned portable download github
text: Install the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (x64), once per PC. If it's missing, Windows offers the download when vyberun starts. Download the latest vyberun-<version>-win-x64.zip from Releases . Unzip it to a folder that stays, for example C:\Tools , and run vyberun\vyberun.exe . Warning. The zip isn't signed. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", choose More info , then Run anyway . If Smart App Control is on, Windows may block the zip's vyberun altogether: use the Store version instead. Each release lists a SHA-256 checksum for its zip, so you can check the download. Tip. Don't run vyberun from your Downloads folder. Downloads tends to get cleaned up, and each vyberun folder keeps its own tabs (see Common problems ).

head: The first start
text: The first time vyberun starts, Help opens on a one-minute tour. You can open it again any time from Help ▸ How to use vyberun . Then add the folder you work in: click + next to General in the sidebar ▸ Add folder… , or drag the folder from File Explorer onto the sidebar. It becomes a card. Click the card and a terminal opens in that folder.

head: Where your settings live
text: Your settings, spaces, cards and servers are kept in %LOCALAPPDATA%\vyberun , not in the program's folder, so updating vyberun keeps them. Help ▸ Open vyberun's settings folder opens it. Saved server passwords are kept in Windows Credential Manager. See Files vyberun uses for the details.
Keep vyberun up to date, or remove it and its settings.

head: Which version you have
text: Help ▸ About vyberun shows the version. Every release and what changed in it is on the Releases page .

head: Updating the Store version
text: The Microsoft Store updates vyberun by itself. To update now, open the Store's Downloads page and choose Get updates . Warning. An update closes vyberun, including the background program that keeps your tabs running, so tabs that were running end. Finish or save what's running before you update.

head: Updating the zip
text: Download the new zip from Releases . Close vyberun. Choosing Keep running is fine: your tabs keep running while you update. Unzip the new version over the old one, into the same folder, replacing the files. Start vyberun. Your tabs, settings, spaces and servers are as they were. Note. Unzip into the same folder as before. vyberun in a different folder has its own background program, so it wouldn't show the tabs the old folder's vyberun kept running.

head: Moving from the zip to the Store version
kw: switch migrate store zip settings kept
text: Close the zip's vyberun with Stop everything : tabs it kept running don't move to the Store version. Install the Store version, from the Microsoft Store or with winget install vyberun . Start it. It finds your spaces, cards, servers and settings where the zip left them. If you had set vyberun up for Claude Code, the Store version moves that setup to its own tools by itself. Delete the zip's folder.

head: Uninstalling
text: Close vyberun. In the close dialog, choose Stop everything , so nothing keeps running. Remove the program: - Store version: right-click vyberun in the Start menu ▸ Uninstall . - Zip: delete the folder you unzipped it into. To remove your settings too, delete %LOCALAPPDATA%\vyberun if it's there. The Store version installed on a PC that never had vyberun keeps them inside its own folder instead, and Windows removes them with it (see Files vyberun uses ). To remove saved server passwords, open Windows Credential Manager ▸ Windows Credentials and remove the entries named vyberun server … . If you set vyberun up for Claude Code (the checklist's Fix ), take that out of Claude Code too, or Claude Code reports a failed hook at every start: - Run claude mcp remove --scope user vyberun . - In %USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json , delete the four hooks that run vyberun-agents.exe , and leave the rest of the file as it is. Uninstalling doesn't touch your projects or your servers.
The parts of vyberun's window, and what each one is for. The title bar with its search open, the sidebar on the left, a tab split into two panes on the right.

head: The title bar
kw: menu search memory cpu full screen
text: From left to right: The menus: File, View, Terminal, Extensions and Help. With Settings ▸ Title bar ▸ Show the full menu bar off, they open from the vyberun logo instead. The search box. Searches files and folders on your PC ( Files ) or everything in vyberun ( vyberun ): tabs, cards, servers and settings. Tab switches between the two. Ctrl + Shift + P opens it. See Find and search . The sidebar button ( Ctrl + Shift + B ) shows or hides the sidebar. Full screen ( F11 ) shows just the terminal. Esc leaves it.

head: The sidebar
text: Your work, on the left: Search spaces , at the top, filters the sidebar as you type. Beside it: ◷ shows only the cards you worked in recently (the last hour, today, the last 7 days or a date range), ⇅ changes the order of the cards (your own order, recent first, or oldest first), and + makes a new space. Spaces group your cards, for example one space per ticket or client. Each space has a coloured header that sums up what runs in it, such as "1 waiting · 2 working", even when it's folded. New cards land in General . Cards are your projects and terminals. A card's tabs are listed under it, with each tab's role and when it was last used. Servers , at the bottom: your SSH servers, one card each. Hold Ctrl and drag to move a card or a space. Drag the sidebar's edge to make it wider.

head: The tab row
text: Above the terminal: the tabs of the card you're in. Each tab shows its name, its role if it has one, and a dot for its state: working, waiting for you, or finished. + opens a new tab in the card's folder, in your default shell. The small arrow next to it picks another shell (Git Bash, PowerShell, Command Prompt or Ubuntu) and brings back detached tabs. Double-click a tab to rename it, and drag it to move it. Right-click it for its menu: give it a role ( Set role… ), move it to another card and more. On the right of the tab row, the memory and CPU used by vyberun and everything in its tabs. Click it to open Terminal ▸ Activity… .

head: The terminal
text: The rest of the window is the terminal, drawn by the same renderer as Windows Terminal. A tab can be split into panes, side by side or one above the other. See Sessions that survive for what happens to it when you close vyberun.
Each card has its own tabs, in the shell you like.

head: Opening a tab
text: Click + above the terminal. A new tab opens in the card's folder, in your default shell. For another shell, click the small arrow next to + and choose Git Bash , PowerShell , Command Prompt or Ubuntu . Terminal ▸ New tab offers the same, and PowerShell as administrator . That one opens in its own window, after Windows asks: a tab inside vyberun can't run as administrator.

head: Shells
kw: git bash powershell cmd wsl ubuntu default
text: Shell What it needs PowerShell Nothing: it comes with Windows. Command Prompt Nothing. Git Bash Git for Windows . Ubuntu WSL with Ubuntu: wsl --install in an administrator PowerShell. To choose the shell new tabs open, go to Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ New tabs ▸ Shell . It's used by + , by a project's first tab and by Open in Terminal . The arrow next to + still offers the others.

head: Naming, moving and colouring tabs
text: Rename: double-click the tab and type a name. Move: drag the tab along the tab row. Colour: right-click the tab ▸ Color . Mark a server tab red or a Claude tab purple, for example. The colour stays after a restart. Role: right-click the tab ▸ Set role… . A role tells an agent in that tab what it does, such as "Tester: checks against the ticket". A tab's dot shows its state: a command is running, an agent is working, it's waiting for you, or it has finished.

head: Closing a tab
text: Click the tab's ✕ . A program still running in it is ended the normal way first, as Ctrl + C would. The ✕ is easy to hit by accident. Turn on Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Closing a tab ▸ Ask before closing a tab and vyberun asks first: close it, keep it running out of sight, or cancel. To put a tab away without closing it, see Sessions that survive .

head: Text size
text: Keys Does Ctrl + = Bigger text Ctrl + - Smaller text Ctrl + 0 Back to the default size View ▸ Terminal text size and Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Text do the same.

head: Long commands
text: When a command that ran over 10 seconds finishes while you're in another tab or another program, Windows shows a notification. Turn it off in Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Long commands .

head: Moving around the history
text: In Git Bash and Ubuntu, vyberun knows where each command starts: Ctrl + ↑ and Ctrl + ↓ jump to the previous or next command. Ctrl + Shift + O copies one command's output. Both are in the Terminal menu too.
Several terminals in one tab, or several tabs side by side.

head: Splitting a tab
kw: split pane side by side right down
text: Keys Splits Ctrl + Shift + D To the right Ctrl + Shift + S Downward Ctrl + Shift + A To the left Ctrl + Shift + W Upward The new pane opens in the same folder, and it's the one you type in. In a server tab, it opens a new connection to the same server, in the folder you were in. Terminal ▸ Split offers the same. Tip. If your typing suddenly goes somewhere else, a split may have opened by accident. Close it with Ctrl + Shift + Q .

head: Working with panes
text: Move between panes: Alt and the arrow keys. A coloured outline shows the pane you're in. Zoom a pane to fill the tab: Ctrl + Shift + Z . Press it again to see them all. Close a pane: Ctrl + Shift + Q . The others take its room. Resize: drag the line between two panes. Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Split panes ▸ Dim unfocused panes makes the panes you're not typing in dimmer.

head: Moving a pane elsewhere
text: Hold Ctrl and right-click the pane ▸ Move : Into tab puts it in another tab. To project sends it to another card, still running.

head: Tab groups
text: A group shows several tabs side by side, and stands for them in the tab row as one tab. Each tab stays as it is: its panes, its name and what runs in it. Hold Ctrl and click the tabs you want. The one you're on counts too. Press Ctrl + Shift + G . They fold into one group tab and show side by side. Click a tile's bar to type in it. Ctrl + Shift + Z makes that tile fill the view, and again shows them all. A tile's ✕ takes that tab out of the group. It keeps running. Double-click the group tab to rename it. Right-click it for Color and Ungroup . Click another tab and the group waits as its tab. Groups stay after a restart. A group holds up to 6 tabs. Change it in Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Tab groups (2 to 9). Above 6, each terminal gets small: best on a large or second monitor.
Close vyberun and your tabs keep running. Open it again and they're back, further along.

head: Closing vyberun
text: vyberun's tabs don't run inside its window. Each tab's shell runs in a separate background program, the session host, so closing the window doesn't stop them. A build, a server or a Claude Code session keeps going while vyberun is closed. Close vyberun. If tabs are open, it asks what to do with them: Keep running , Stop everything or Cancel . Choose Keep running . Your tabs carry on in the background. Open vyberun again, or click its icon in the notification area of the taskbar. Your tabs come back with everything they printed meanwhile. Restart vyberun in the File menu always keeps the tabs.

head: Choosing what closing does
kw: ask each time remember my choice
text: Tick Remember my choice in the close dialog, or open Settings ▸ Closing vyberun and pick one: Choice When vyberun closes with tabs open Ask each time vyberun asks (the default). Keep them running in the background The window closes; every tab keeps running. Stop everything Every tab's program is stopped, then vyberun closes. Stopping ends running programs the normal way first, as Ctrl + C would, so nothing is cut off in the middle of writing a file.

head: What's still running
text: While vyberun is closed, its icon in the notification area says how many tabs run in the background. Click it to open vyberun. Right-click it for Open vyberun or Stop everything… . While vyberun is open, the memory and CPU next to the tabs count vyberun and everything in its tabs. They turn amber when this PC runs low on memory. Click them, or choose Terminal ▸ Activity… , to see each tab's share and stop what you don't need.

head: Putting a tab away
text: To clear the tab row without stopping a tab, detach it. It keeps running inside vyberun, out of view. Press Ctrl + Shift + X in the tab. To bring it back, click the small arrow next to + above the terminal and choose it, or hold Ctrl and right-click a tab ▸ Re-attach tab .

head: What ends a session
text: Tabs keep running until one of these happens: Windows restarts, shuts down or signs you out. You stop them: Stop everything , closing a tab, or Stop in Activity. The program in the tab exits, for example when you type exit . The Store updates vyberun (see Updating and uninstalling ). Warning. A restart for Windows Update ends your tabs too. Save your work before one.

head: On a server
text: A server tab's work can keep running on the server itself, even with your PC off: close the tab with Leave it running on the server , then rejoin it later with ▶ on the server's card. This uses the server's own tmux; nothing is installed.
Two searches: inside the tab you're in, and everywhere.

head: Find in a tab
kw: find text ctrl shift f history match
text: Press Ctrl + Shift + F . The find bar opens over the tab row. Type what you're looking for. It searches the tab's whole history, not just the screen. Enter or ↑ goes to an older match, Shift + Enter or ↓ to a newer one. Esc closes the bar. The bar's Match case button makes upper and lower case count.

head: Find in a Claude Code conversation
text: Claude Code redraws its screen, so most of a long conversation isn't in the terminal any more. In a Claude tab, Ctrl + Shift + F searches Claude's whole conversation instead: Press Ctrl + Shift + F in the Claude tab and type. Press Enter . vyberun shows the conversation with the matches, even what's long gone from the screen. Esc goes back to Claude.

head: Search everywhere
kw: ctrl shift p files folders everything
text: The search box in the title bar searches two things. Tab switches between them. Files: files and folders on your PC, by name: what Windows has indexed, plus your projects' folders. Results show as you type. vyberun: your tabs, cards, servers, snippets, commands, settings and Help's pages. Press Ctrl + Shift + P to go to it from anywhere.

head: In the results
text: Keys Does Enter Opens it: a file in its app, a folder in File Explorer, a tab or card in vyberun. On a setting, switches it. Shift + Enter Files and folders: opens a new terminal there Ctrl + Enter Files: shows it in File Explorer Esc Leaves the search

head: Search tips
text: Words match in any order: checkout request finds CheckoutRequest.php . * or % stands for anything in between: cust%test finds CustomerTest.php , report*2024 finds report-march-2024.pdf . Windows doesn't index some folders, such as AppData. Add them in Settings ▸ Search ▸ Also search these folders and vyberun searches them too.

head: Recent cards
text: Ctrl + Shift + R lists your cards, the most recent first. Hold Ctrl + Shift , tap R to go down the list, and let go to open the card.
Copy and paste text, paths and pictures, and open links and files from the terminal.

head: Copy and paste
kw: copy paste clipboard ctrl shift c
text: Keys Does Ctrl + Shift + C Copies the highlighted text Ctrl + V Pastes Right-click Copies the highlighted text, or pastes when nothing is highlighted Ctrl +right-click Opens the terminal's menu: copy, paste, split, screenshot and more Drag to highlight text. To swap what right-click and Ctrl +right-click do, go to Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Mouse ▸ Right-click in a terminal . Tip. Typed too much? Highlight part of the line you're typing and press Backspace or Delete : all of the highlighted part goes at once.

head: Pasting a file's path
text: Copy a file in File Explorer, then press Ctrl + V in the terminal: its full path is typed for you. Or drag files from File Explorer onto the terminal. In Git Bash and Ubuntu, a Windows path such as C:\Users\dev\notes.txt goes in the way that shell writes it, /c/Users/dev/notes.txt , since bash drops backslashes.

head: Pasting a picture
text: Take a screenshot with the Snipping Tool ( Win + Shift + S ), then press Ctrl + V in the terminal. vyberun saves the picture as an image file and types its path, so a program such as Claude Code can open it.

head: Opening links and files
text: Hold Ctrl and click a link or a file path in the terminal: A link opens in your browser. A code or text file opens in your editor, at its line where the editor can. Choose the editor in Settings ▸ Projects ▸ Open projects in . Other files open in the app Windows uses for them.
Turn what's in a terminal into a picture, mark it up and share it.

head: A screenshot of some lines
kw: ctrl shift i picture image capture
text: Highlight the lines. Press Ctrl + Shift + I . The picture is copied, and its preview opens so you can mark it up.

head: A long screenshot
kw: ctrl shift k long whole scroll
text: For more than fits on the screen: drag past the bottom of the window (it scrolls as you go), then press Ctrl + Shift + K . Everything you highlighted becomes one picture.

head: In Claude Code
text: Claude Code redraws its screen, so there are two ways: Only what's on Claude's screen, with collapsed output left collapsed: Highlight a line or two where the picture should start, and press Ctrl + Shift + K . The start is marked. Scroll to where it should end, highlight a line or two there, and press Ctrl + Shift + K again. Wait while the screen is dimmed: vyberun scrolls Claude's view from one to the other and joins it. To take just what's highlighted on the screen, press Ctrl + Shift + K twice without highlighting anything new in between. Everything, with the commands' full output: With nothing highlighted, press Ctrl + Shift + I . Screenshot mode puts the whole conversation in the terminal, even what Claude's screen hides. Highlight any part, as long as you like. Enter takes it. Esc goes back to Claude without one.

head: In a server tab
text: In a server tab, Ctrl + Shift + I with nothing highlighted brings the tab's whole history from the server, so you can highlight past the screen. This works when the server keeps it with tmux. A server you sign in to with a password can't be asked this way: hold Shift and drag to highlight what's on screen.

head: Marking it up
kw: pen highlighter box circle crop eraser annotate
text: In the preview: Key Tool P Pen H Highlighter R Box O Circle E Eraser C Crop: drag around the part that matters Ctrl + Z Undo the last mark or crop To look around a picture larger than the window, hold V or Ctrl and drag. Ctrl + = , Ctrl + - , Ctrl + 0 and Ctrl + 1 zoom in, zoom out, fit the window and show it at actual size.

head: Copying and saving
text: Ctrl + C copies the picture with your marks. Paste it anywhere, or straight into Claude Code. Ctrl + S saves it as a PNG file. Esc closes the preview. Settings ▸ Screenshots ▸ Frame the screenshots puts a soft frame and shadow around them. The preview's Framed and Plain switch does the same for one picture.
Group your projects, terminals and servers the way you work. Two spaces, one per ticket. A card's tabs are listed under it with their roles.

head: Spaces
kw: group folder ticket client new space
text: A space is a group of cards, for example one per ticket, client or product. Make as many as you like. Click + at the top of the sidebar, next to Search spaces . Name the space. Put cards in it: hold Ctrl and drag a card onto it, or click ⋯ on the card ▸ Move to space . General and Servers are built-in spaces: new cards land there, and they can't be renamed or deleted. Once you have spaces of your own, General shows only while it has cards in it. Server cards can go in your spaces too. Fold a space: click its name. The card you're in stays in view. Reorder spaces: hold Ctrl and drag a space's name. Colour a space: right-click its name ▸ Color . Its header is tinted with it. Rename or delete it: right-click its name. Deleting a space puts its cards back where they came from: projects in General , servers in Servers . Each space's header sums up what runs in its cards, such as "1 waiting · 2 working", even when it's folded. Click the summary to go there.

head: Cards
text: A card is a project folder, a server, or a set of terminals. Click it and its tabs open, just as you left them. Under it, each tab is listed with its role and when you last worked in it ( 25m ). Cards you haven't touched today are dimmed. ⋯ on a card opens its menu: Item Does Run Runs one of the project's commands (see Projects ) Open in … Opens the project in your editor Open Folder Opens it in File Explorer Open in Terminal Opens a new tab in its folder Combine with… Puts two related folders in one card, such as a backend and its frontend Color Writes the card's name in a colour Icon Puts a picture of your own (PNG, JPG or ICO) beside its name Links Keeps links with the card, such as its ticket or its pull request Pin to top Keeps it at the top of its space Move to space Moves it to another space Remove from list Takes it out of vyberun. The folder and its files stay where they are. To move a card, hold Ctrl and drag it. A card with links shows a link icon next to its name: click it to open them.

head: Terminals without a project
text: Not everything belongs to a project. Click + next to a space's name ▸ New terminal… for a card that just holds terminals.

head: Finding your way
kw: recent today last hour filter sort search spaces
text: Search spaces , at the top of the sidebar, filters it as you type. ◷ next to it shows only the cards you worked in within the last hour, today, the last 7 days, or the dates you pick. Each card stays in its own space. Its × shows everything again. ⇅ sorts each space's cards: your own order, the most recent first, or the oldest first. Ctrl + Shift + R lists your cards, the most recent first (see Find and search ).

head: Archiving a space
text: Done with a ticket? Right-click its space's name ▸ Archive space . It leaves the sidebar with its cards. To find it again, open View ▸ Sidebar ▸ Archived spaces… . Search by a space's or a card's name, and choose Restore to bring it back.

head: The sidebar itself
text: Ctrl + Shift + B hides or shows the sidebar. Drag its edge to make it wider or narrower. Hold Ctrl and scroll over it to make everything in it bigger or smaller. Settings ▸ Sidebar has more: compact cards on one line, and which parts are shown.
Any folder can be a project, with its own tabs and commands.

head: Adding a project
text: Click + next to General , or next to one of your spaces' names to add it straight there. Choose Add folder… and pick the folder. Or drag the folder from File Explorer onto the sidebar. Settings ▸ Projects ▸ Add folder does the same.

head: What a card shows
kw: type branch git laravel node react
text: Its type beside its name, such as node , laravel or .net , found from the files in the folder. Its git branch under it. Its tabs, each with its role and when you last worked in it. With Settings ▸ Sidebar ▸ Compact cards on, a project takes one line; its branch and folder show when you hover its name.

head: Running its commands
kw: npm scripts artisan dotnet python run command
text: You don't have to type a project's usual commands: Click ⋯ on the card ▸ Run . Choose a command. vyberun lists what it found in the folder: npm scripts, artisan, dotnet, Python and more. It runs in a new tab of that card.

head: Opening it elsewhere
kw: editor vs code cursor phpstorm explorer
text: ⋯ on the card has: Open in your editor: VS Code, Cursor, PhpStorm and others. Choose which in Settings ▸ Projects ▸ Open projects in . The same editor opens files you Ctrl +click in the terminal. Open Folder : File Explorer. Open in Terminal : a new tab in the folder.

head: Several folders in one card
text: When folders belong together, such as an API and its web front end, click ⋯ on one card ▸ Combine with… , tick the others and give the card a name. They show as one card, whose tabs can be in any of its folders, and its Open in offers each folder or all of them. This is only in vyberun: each folder stays where it is.

head: Removing a project
text: ⋯ on the card ▸ Remove from list takes it out of vyberun. The folder and its files stay where they are. See Spaces and cards for everything else a card can do.
See what's working, what needs you, and what it costs.

head: A tab's state
kw: working waiting done failed dot status colour
text: Each tab, in the tab row and in the sidebar, shows how it's going: Shown Means Amber Waiting for you: an agent asks a question or needs your permission Accent colour Working: an agent or a command is busy Green Finished while you were elsewhere Red Failed Nothing Idle An agent counts as working while it waits on a long command or on its own background agents too. Each space's header sums up its cards, most pressing first, such as "1 waiting · 2 working".

head: Notifications
text: When something needs you while you're in another tab or another program, Windows shows a notification, and vyberun's taskbar button flashes until you come back: A Claude needs you, or has finished, with how long it worked. One of Claude's subagents has finished. A command that ran over 10 seconds has finished or failed. Turn this off in Settings ▸ Terminal ▸ Long commands . Claude tabs stopped messaging each other, because they kept going without you (see Roles and handovers ). Windows' own notification settings ( Settings ▸ System ▸ Notifications ) decide whether and how they show, as for any program.

head: Memory and CPU
kw: memory ram cpu usage title bar amber
text: Next to the tabs, vyberun shows the memory and CPU used by itself and everything in its tabs, read every few seconds. It turns amber when this PC is low on memory.

head: Activity
kw: activity task manager stop running programs idle claude
text: Click the memory and CPU, or choose Terminal ▸ Activity… . It lists everything running in vyberun's tabs: Each pane's Claude Code, command, service or shell, with its memory, its CPU now, and how long it's been running. Programs left running after their tab closed, such as a dev server an agent started in the background. vyberun's own share, apart. Go to opens that tab. Stop ends one, the way Ctrl + C would, and the tab stays open. Stop all ends everything listed. A Claude tab that has been idle for a long time is marked, so you can stop the ones you've finished with.
Your servers in the sidebar, one click from a terminal on them.

head: Adding a server
text: Click + next to Servers in the sidebar. Fill in Name , Host , Port and User (such as deploy or admin ). Under Sign in with , choose Key file , Password or PuTTY session . See Keys and PuTTY sessions . Choose Save . The server becomes a card in Servers . To change it later: ⋯ on its card ▸ Edit . Server cards can be moved into your own spaces like any other card.

head: Signing in with a password
text: Type it in the Password box and tick Remember it . When the server asks for it, vyberun types it for you. It's kept by Windows Credential Manager, never in vyberun's files. Leave the box empty to type the password yourself in the tab each time.

head: Connecting
text: Click ▶ on the server's card. A tab opens on the server, and the card's dot turns green. Dot Means Green Connected Blue Your work is still running on the server, with no tab open (see tmux sessions ) Red The connection was lost. Press Enter in the tab to connect again. Grey No tab open Split a server tab ( Ctrl + Shift + D and the other split keys) and the new pane connects to the same server, in the folder you were in.

head: Production servers
text: Tick Production server when adding one. Its card and tabs are marked PROD , so you always know where you are. vyberun is more careful there too: an upload asks first, and agents always ask before reading or investigating its tabs.

head: Snippets
text: Save the commands you run often on a server: ⋯ on its card ▸ Snippets . Write {name} in a snippet and vyberun asks for that value each time it runs, for example tail -n 200 /var/log/{service}.log .

head: What vyberun changes on a server
text: Nothing. vyberun connects over SSH like any other client and uses only what's already there: the shell, and tmux if the server has it. It never installs anything or changes the server's settings.

head: Settings
text: Settings ▸ Servers can forget every remembered password, and every "Remember my choice" answer (what closing a server's tab does, and where a PuTTY server opens), so you're asked again.
Sign in to servers with a key file or the sessions you saved in PuTTY.

head: Key files
kw: ssh key pem ppk openssh private key
text: Under Sign in with , choose Key file , then Browse… to the key. vyberun takes: .pem and OpenSSH keys, as most cloud providers and ssh-keygen make them. .ppk keys, PuTTY's own format. These need PuTTY installed, since vyberun signs in with them through PuTTY's plink . A key stays where it is: vyberun remembers its path and reads it when it connects.

head: Keys with a passphrase
text: vyberun connects without asking you questions, so a .ppk key with a passphrase needs converting once: Open it in PuTTYgen. The server's form has an Open in PuTTYgen button. Choose Conversions ▸ Export OpenSSH key and save it next to the .ppk . Browse… to the new key in the server's form.

head: PuTTY sessions
text: If you've saved sessions in PuTTY, vyberun can use them: The PuTTY button next to + in Servers brings in all of them at once, one card each. Or add one server: under Sign in with , choose PuTTY session and pick it. Its address, user and key come from PuTTY. Some sessions don't keep everything vyberun needs: No user name: fill in User . Tabs and file copies sign in as that user. No address: type the host, user and key under Key file instead. Opens in chooses where a PuTTY session's server opens: a vyberun tab, or Ask each time . ⋯ on its card ▸ Open in PuTTY opens it in PuTTY's own window.

head: When signing in fails
text: "login as:" in a copy or a tab: the PuTTY session has no user name. Fill in User in the server's form. Permission denied: the server doesn't accept that key or user. Check them with ssh -i <key> <user>@<host> in a PowerShell tab. See Common problems for copies that stop with "Cannot answer interactive prompts".
Leave your work running on the server, and pick it up later, even after your PC restarts.

head: Keeping your work running
kw: tmux keep running disconnect background server
text: vyberun can run a server tab's shell inside the server's own tmux. Then your work doesn't depend on the connection: close the tab, shut down your PC, and it carries on there. Tick Keep my work running on the server in the server's form. That's all: vyberun uses the tmux the server already has, and installs nothing. A server without tmux gets a plain shell, and vyberun says so.

head: Leaving and rejoining
text: Close the server's tab and choose Leave it running on the server . The card's dot turns blue: your work goes on there. Later, click ▶ on the card and choose Rejoin . The tab comes back as it is now on the server. Remember my choice in that dialog skips the question next time. Settings ▸ Servers forgets the answer again. Note. This is separate from vyberun's own Sessions that survive . Those keep tabs running on your PC while vyberun is closed, and end when Windows restarts. tmux keeps work running on the server, which doesn't care what your PC does.

head: Memory and CPU
text: The Servers section shows each server's tmux sessions with the memory and CPU they use. The CPU figure is the average since each program started, not what it uses this moment.

head: A server tab's history
text: tmux keeps a tab's history on the server, not in the tab. To select, search or screenshot past the screen, press Ctrl + Shift + I with nothing highlighted: vyberun brings the whole history from the server. See Screenshots .
Copy files to and from a server without leaving the terminal.

head: From a server
text: Hold Ctrl and click a file's name in the server's tab. File names are underlined while Ctrl is held. vyberun checks with the server that it's a file, then offers where it goes: the place your last download went (first in the list: Enter takes it), a local tab (into the folder it's in), Downloads, or any folder. A highlighted path works too: Ctrl +right-click ▸ Download to .

head: To a server
kw: upload put send file to server drop
text: Drop files on the server's tab. They go into the folder that tab is in. Or Ctrl +right-click in the server's tab ▸ Upload a file here… . Or, in a local tab, highlight a file's name and Ctrl +right-click ▸ Upload to ▸ a server. It goes into the folder that server's tab is in, or, with Choose a server… , its home folder. Folders can't be uploaded as they are: right-click the folder in File Explorer ▸ Compress to ZIP and drop the zip. When a file of that name is already there, vyberun asks: keep both (the new one saved as name-1 ) or replace it. On a production server , every upload asks first.

head: While it copies
text: A line under the terminal shows the progress, with Pause and Cancel . If the connection drops, what's copied so far is kept, and vyberun tries again by itself, carrying on from there. A resumed copy is checked against the original (SHA-256) before it gets its name, so a file is never half right. Closed vyberun in the middle of a copy? It's offered again when vyberun starts: Resume or Discard . Copies sign in the same way as the server's tabs: its key or its remembered password.
vyberun is made for working with Claude Code. Start it in a tab and vyberun follows what it does.

head: Starting Claude
text: Open a project's card. Type claude in its tab and press Enter . Claude Code starts in that folder, and keeps running when you close vyberun (see Sessions that survive ). vyberun doesn't install Claude Code or sign you in: install it as Anthropic describes, once, and it works in any tab.

head: Setting it up for vyberun
kw: setup checklist fix settings mcp tools
text: A few Claude Code settings make it work better inside vyberun: the mouse, copying, screenshots, and vyberun's tools for reading tabs. Open Settings ▸ Claude Code ▸ Open the checklist… . Choose Fix next to anything that isn't set. Start Claude again in the tabs where it was already running. Claude Code reads its settings and tools when it starts. The checklist also starts vyberun's tools once, to be sure they run: if they're set up but don't start, it says so, with the reason. What Fix adds to Claude Code's settings, and how to take it out again: Files vyberun uses .

head: Seeing what Claude does
kw: working waiting finished blink dot amber
text: You can tell what each Claude is doing from any tab: A dot blinks on its tab while Claude works. An amber ! shows when Claude waits for you: a question or a permission request. When it finishes while you're elsewhere, its line in the sidebar blinks green until you open it. In a folded space, the space's name blinks. In the sidebar, a card's tabs are listed under it: ✳ for a Claude tab, >_ for a shell, then the tab's name and its role. Click a line to go to that tab. When vyberun isn't in front, Windows tells you when Claude needs you or has finished (see Notifications and activity ).

head: Showing Claude something from another tab
text: An error in a server's tab or a build? Give it to Claude without copying: Highlight the lines, then Ctrl +right-click ▸ Show selection to an agent . Or right-click the tab ▸ Show to an agent for its last command or last lines. Pick an agent tab: Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex or Aider. The text lands in that agent's prompt, with where it came from. Nothing is sent until you press Enter , so add your question first. To let Claude look around a broken tab itself, see Reading other tabs .

head: Moving a conversation
kw: move claude another tab card resume
text: A Claude conversation belongs in another tab or card? Right-click its tab ▸ Move Claude to… and pick where. The conversation moves, not the terminal: it's resumed there, with its role.

head: Finding and capturing
text: Ctrl + Shift + F in a Claude tab searches its whole conversation, even what's long gone from the screen. See Find and search . Ctrl + Shift + K captures a long answer as one picture. See Screenshots .

head: Other agents
text: vyberun recognises Claude Code best: its state, its conversation, its tools. Other command-line agents such as Gemini CLI, Codex and Aider run in tabs like any program, can be given a role, and can be shown text from other tabs. Messages between agents, handovers and reading tabs are Claude Code only for now.
Several Claude tabs working as a team: each with a role, handing work to each other. Three tabs with roles: backend, frontend and qa.

head: Giving a tab a role
kw: role set role backend frontend tester team
text: Right-click the tab ▸ Set role… . Type what the agent in it does, for example "Backend: Laravel API" or "Tester: checks against the ticket". The role shows on the tab and in the sidebar. A Claude started in that tab is told its role, and the other Claude tabs with theirs, so it knows who does what and who to hand work to ("hand the UI part to @fe"). Other agents, such as Gemini CLI or Codex, get their role in their prompt when you set it. A Claude that's already running learns a changed role from your next message to it.

head: Handovers
text: Settings ▸ Agents ▸ Handovers decides when an agent may hand part of its work to another agent tab: Choice The agent Only when I ask Hands work over only when you tell it to. The default. Suggest first, I say yes Tells you when a part fits a teammate better, and hands it over once you agree. On its own Hands parts over itself and carries the task through, coming back when it's done or needs your decision. Drive it to the end Asks teammates rather than you about what they own, and comes back only for what can't be undone, such as a commit or a deploy. Best with a loop guard of 20. Whatever you choose, a Claude asked something by a teammate answers that teammate.

head: Messages between tabs
kw: agent messages arrow sent received pause
text: When Claude tabs message each other, the tab's line in the sidebar shows it for half a minute: → fe (it sent fe a message) or ← be (it heard from be). Right-click a tab ▸ Agent messages… lists every message since vyberun started. From there you can also pause messages between Claude tabs altogether.

head: The loop guard
kw: loop stopped paused too many messages
text: Agents could keep messaging each other without you. After 10 messages between them since you last typed in a Claude tab, vyberun stops the next one: that Claude is told to tell you where things stand, and its line says ⏸ stopped . Windows notifies you too. Typing in any Claude tab lets them go on. Choose the number in Settings ▸ Agents ▸ Loop guard : 5, 10, 20 or off. A Claude's messages to its own subagents don't count.

head: Saved agents
text: Use the same roles on every ticket? Save them: Settings ▸ Agents ▸ Add an agent… , or tick Save as an agent in Set role… . Next time, Set role… offers your saved agents in one click. {card} in a role becomes the card's name. A saved agent can also bring its own instructions file, Claude Code settings file, a guard script that blocks commands you don't want run, and skills (see Subagents and skills ). ⋯ on a card ▸ Start agent opens a tab with it already running.
Let Claude read your other tabs, or investigate a broken one, with your permission.

head: Reading a tab
kw: read tab list_tabs read_tab mcp tools
text: With vyberun's tools set up (see Claude in a tab ), a Claude can see your tabs and read one. Just ask: "read the api tab" or "what's the error in the build tab?". Claude doesn't have to be told which tab is which: it can list them with their names, cards and roles. Reading never types anything into the tab. Every read is written to vyberun.log . Note. Claude Code loads its tools when it starts. A Claude started before vyberun set them up can't read tabs until you start it again in its tab.

head: Who decides
text: Settings ▸ Agents ▸ Reading other tabs: Choice Reading a tab Ask every time Every read asks: Allow once or No . Ask once per tab The first read of a tab asks. Always for this tab lasts until vyberun closes. The default. This PC's tabs freely Tabs on this PC are read without asking. A server's tab asks once per tab. All tabs freely Every tab is read without asking, server tabs too. A production server's tab asks every time, whatever you choose.

head: Letting an agent investigate
kw: investigate debug broken tab commands look
text: Something broken in a tab, such as a server, a dev server or a build? Let an agent look into it: Right-click the tab ▸ Let an agent investigate ▸ pick a Claude Code tab. The agent gets the tab's output, then reads it without asking, and runs commands that only look: a log, a service's status, a folder, git's state. Each command shows in the tab as it runs. A command that changes something, or stopping what runs there, shows you a dialog first with the agent's reason. You can change the command, allow it, or refuse. A bar above the terminal says who is investigating. Done on it ends that. Closing either tab ends it too. On a production server's tab, every command asks, and nothing that changes something runs there.

head: What reading can't do
text: An agent can't type into a tab it reads. Only an investigation runs commands, and only as described above. A Claude proves which tab it's in with a key of its own, so one tab's Claude can't pretend to be another's. Text read from a server or a terminal is never put into a command unchecked.
Follow a Claude's own agents as they work, and give an agent skills of its own.

head: Subagents in the sidebar
kw: subagents agents claude agents folder sidebar
text: A Claude can run agents of its own, defined in its project's .claude/agents . They run inside that one Claude tab, with no extra terminals. While they work, vyberun gives each a line under the Claude tab in the sidebar: what it's doing now, and for how long. A finished one says done for a few minutes afterwards.

head: Following one
kw: panel follow read only files commands
text: Click a subagent's line to follow its work beside the terminal: what it was asked, the files it read and changed, the commands it ran and what came back. The panel is read only: nothing is sent to the agent. Esc or ✕ closes it.

head: New and stuck
text: new: it finished while you were elsewhere. If vyberun isn't in front and notifications for long commands are on, Windows tells you too. stuck? in amber: it keeps hitting the same wall, such as commands blocked by a hook, the same command again and again, errors in a row, or a long silence. Its panel says why.

head: Skills
text: A saved agent can bring skills: instructions Claude Code loads for that tab alone. Open Settings ▸ Agents and edit the saved agent. Add .md or .zip files… : a .md is a skill itself, a .zip is a skill's folder. Start the agent on a card ( ⋯ ▸ Start agent ). Its skills are there in that tab. Edit a skill's file any time, in any editor: an agent started afterwards reads the new version.
Extensions add their own spaces, menus and services to vyberun.

head: What an extension is
text: An extension teaches vyberun about a kind of work: for example a space that lists your Docker Compose stacks, or one that shows what's listening on which port. It can add its own space to the sidebar with cards, buttons and menus, its own menu in the menu bar, and run things in vyberun's terminal. Extensions add to vyberun. They never change vyberun itself.

head: Turning them on and off
text: Open Extensions ▸ Manage extensions… . It lists what's installed, with any problem loading one. Turn each on or off any time: its part of vyberun comes and goes right away. To hide an extension's space without turning it off, use Settings ▸ Sidebar .

head: Adding one someone shared
text: Extensions ▸ Manage extensions… ▸ Add .zip… (or Add folder… ). vyberun shows who made it and asks before running it. Warning. An extension runs code with your rights, like any program you install. Only turn on extensions you trust.

head: Where they're kept
text: Extensions ▸ Open my extensions folder opens the folder extensions are added to. Removing an extension in Manage extensions… removes it from there. If an extension stops working or vyberun reports a problem with it, turn it off in Manage extensions… : vyberun keeps running either way, and writes the extension's errors to its log (see Logs ).
Make your own extension by describing it to Claude Code. No C# needed.

head: What you need
text: The .NET 10 SDK to build it. dotnet --version should say 10. A coding agent such as Claude Code, to write it for you. You can also write the C# yourself.

head: Making one
text: Extensions ▸ Manage extensions… ▸ New extension… . Give it a name and choose Create . vyberun makes a ready-to-build folder and opens a terminal tab in it. Type claude and describe what it should do (an example follows). Claude writes it and builds it. The build installs it into your extensions folder by itself. Restart vyberun ( File ▸ Restart vyberun , or Ctrl + Shift + F5 ) to load it. The first time, vyberun asks whether to turn it on. For example, in step 2: Make this extension a "Ports" space in vyberun's sidebar: one card per TCP port something is listening on, with the program's name. Each card's menu: Open in browser, Copy URL, and Stop process (ask first). Refresh every 10 seconds. The folder has a CLAUDE.md with the rules and the commands, which Claude reads before it writes anything, so what it builds stays within the rules.

head: Changing it
text: Tell Claude what you'd like different, let it build, then restart vyberun again. vyberun loads an extension's code once, so restart after every build. Extensions ▸ Manage extensions… shows any problem loading it, and vyberun's log has the extension's own lines and errors.

head: Sharing it
text: Zip its folder, with its extension.json . Someone else adds it with Manage extensions… ▸ Add .zip… , and vyberun shows them who made it before it runs.

head: The developer guide
text: The extension developer guide explains the parts of the API, the rules every extension follows, and a ten-minute tutorial that builds the Ports extension above step by step. vyberun has it too: Help ▸ Extension developer guide .
Every key in vyberun, on one page. vyberun shows the same list in Help ▸ All shortcuts .

What each page of vyberun's Settings holds. Open Settings with File ▸ Settings… or Ctrl + , . You can also find any setting from the search: Ctrl + Shift + P , Tab to vyberun , and type its name. Enter on a setting switches it. Each page has Reset to defaults , for that page only. Changes apply at once; there's nothing to save.

head: Each page's Help
text: Pages for a feature have a How does this work? link to its Help page. The settings themselves are stored in vyberun's settings folder (see Files vyberun uses ): change them here, not in the files.
Where vyberun keeps your settings, logs and saved passwords.

head: The settings folder
text: Everything vyberun remembers is in one folder. Where it is depends on how vyberun was installed: Installed The settings folder The zip %LOCALAPPDATA%\vyberun The Store version, on a PC that had the zip before %LOCALAPPDATA%\vyberun , the same folder the zip used The Store version, on a PC that never had vyberun Inside the Store version's own folder: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Packages\Paraxord.vyberun_y91868xpbp6my\LocalCache\Local\vyberun The Store version always sees its folder as %LOCALAPPDATA%\vyberun . On a PC that never had vyberun, Windows keeps that folder inside the app's own folder, and removes it when the app is uninstalled. Help ▸ Open vyberun's settings folder opens it from the zip; for the Store version, paste the path from the table into File Explorer. In it What it holds settings.json and the .txt files Your settings, one value each spaces.json , projects.json , servers.json Your spaces, cards and servers (not their passwords) tabs.json The tabs that are open, so they come back saved-agents.json Your saved agents (Settings ▸ Agents) extensions The extensions you added vyberun.log , session-host.log The logs (see Logs ) session-host A copy of the background program that keeps tabs running agents The zip version's tools for Claude Code (the Store version's are part of the app) Warning. Change settings in vyberun, not in these files. vyberun keeps its settings in memory and writes them all back on the next change, so an edit made while it runs is lost. If you must edit a file, close vyberun first. To move to another PC, copy the folder while vyberun is closed on both. Server passwords don't move with it: enter them again. Note. Moving from the zip to the Store version keeps your spaces, cards, servers and settings: the Store version finds them in %LOCALAPPDATA%\vyberun , where the zip left them, and doesn't start as a first install. To start afresh, close vyberun with Stop everything and rename that folder (to vyberun.old , for example) before starting it; rename it back to return to your old setup.

head: Claude Code's settings
text: When you choose Fix for "Claude works with your vyberun tabs" in the Claude Code checklist, vyberun adds two things to Claude Code's own settings, for every project: Its tools, named vyberun , in %USERPROFILE%\.claude.json ( claude mcp list shows them). Four hooks in %USERPROFILE%\.claude\settings.json : session-start , prompt , may-send and sent , each running vyberun-agents.exe . They point at the zip's copy in the settings folder's agents , or, for the Store version, at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WindowsApps\vyberun-agents.exe , a command the Store version adds to Windows. Outside a vyberun tab they do nothing. A copy of what was there before is kept beside each file ( .vyberun-backup ).

head: Saved passwords
text: When you tick Remember it under a server's password, vyberun keeps it in Windows Credential Manager, not in a file. The entry is named vyberun server … . Open Credential Manager ▸ Windows Credentials to see or remove it.

head: The program folder
text: The zip version runs from the folder you unzipped it into, and nothing in that folder changes while you use it. That's why you can unzip a new version over it. The Store version is installed by Windows in a protected folder.

head: A separate data folder
text: The environment variable VYBERUN_DATA points vyberun at another folder instead of %LOCALAPPDATA%\vyberun , for a test or demo copy that mustn't touch your real settings. Give such a copy its own program folder too: copies of vyberun from the same folder share one background program, and so the same tabs.
The problems people run into most, and how to fix them.

head: "Windows protected your PC"
kw: smartscreen smart app control blocked unsigned warning
text: The zip version isn't signed, so Windows warns the first time it starts. Choose More info , then Run anyway . If Smart App Control blocks it with no way to run it, install vyberun from the Microsoft Store instead: that version is signed by Microsoft. See Installing .

head: vyberun doesn't start: .NET is missing
text: The zip version needs the .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (x64). Windows offers the download when it's missing; you can also get it from Microsoft's .NET page . The Store version includes it.

head: My tabs are gone
text: Tabs survive closing vyberun, but not everything. Check which one happened: Windows restarted, shut down or signed you out. That ends every program, including your tabs. Cards, spaces and servers are kept; open new tabs on them. vyberun was closed with Stop everything , or Settings ▸ Closing vyberun is set to stop them. You started a different copy of vyberun. Each vyberun folder keeps its own tabs. If you unzipped a new version into a new folder, the old folder's vyberun still has the tabs: start that one, and next time unzip over the old folder. The Store updated vyberun. An update ends running tabs. Logs shows how to tell from the logs.

head: Claude Code doesn't see vyberun's tools
text: Claude Code loads its tools when it starts. A Claude started before vyberun set up its tools, or before an update, doesn't have them yet. Quit it ( /exit ) and start it again in the same tab, for example with claude --continue to keep the conversation.

head: Claude Code says "hook failed"
text: Claude Code runs vyberun's hooks at the start of every session and with every message, in any terminal. If they can't run, it shows a red "SessionStart hook failed" or "UserPromptSubmit hook failed". The usual reasons: vyberun was uninstalled, but its setup for Claude Code is still there. Take it out as Uninstalling describes. The Store version 0.1.10. Its tools for Claude couldn't start. Update to 0.1.11 or later: it repairs the setup by itself when it starts, or open the checklist and choose Fix . The checklist ( Settings ▸ Claude Code ▸ Open the checklist… ) says whether vyberun's tools start, and if not, why.

head: vyberun closes while Claude reads a tab
text: Before 0.1.11, vyberun could close by itself while Claude read another tab with nothing highlighted in it. Update vyberun. Your tabs keep running meanwhile: open vyberun again and they're back.

head: Claude says "vyberun isn't answering"
text: Claude's vyberun tools work only while vyberun is open. vyberun was closed, restarting, or had stopped. Open vyberun, then ask Claude again. If it happens while vyberun is open, see Reporting a problem .

head: A Claude tab ignores the mouse
kw: scroll wheel copy select agent view
text: If you can't scroll or select in a Claude Code tab, that Claude is probably running as a background session (Claude Code's Agent View), which takes over the mouse. Stop it with claude stop <its short id> , then claude --resume . Setting "disableAgentView": true in Claude Code's settings avoids it.

head: My typing goes to the wrong place
kw: pane keyboard focus typed claude exited
text: A split pane may have opened by accident: Ctrl + Shift + W , A , S or D splits the tab, and the new pane takes the keyboard. Click the pane you want, or close the new one with Ctrl + Shift + Q .

head: A setting I changed in a file came back
text: vyberun writes all its settings back on the next change, so an edit made in its files while it runs is lost. Change the setting in vyberun, or edit the file with vyberun closed. See Files vyberun uses .

head: Git Bash or Ubuntu isn't offered
text: The shell list shows what's installed. Install Git for Windows for Git Bash, or WSL with Ubuntu ( wsl --install in an administrator PowerShell) for Ubuntu tabs, then restart vyberun.

head: Copying files to a server stops with "Cannot answer interactive prompts"
kw: plink putty copy upload login as passphrase
text: The copy asked a question it can't answer, usually "login as:" (a saved PuTTY session without a user name) or a key's passphrase. Add the user name in the server's settings, or use a key without a passphrase (or load it into Pageant first).
vyberun writes down what it does, so a problem can be traced. The logs are plain text files in vyberun's settings folder (see Files vyberun uses ). They record what vyberun did and when.

head: vyberun.log
text: Help ▸ Open vyberun's log opens it. It records starts and restarts, screenshots, servers, agents and Activity, each line with its time. When something goes wrong, the lines just before it usually say why.

head: session-host.log
text: The background program that keeps your tabs running writes its own log, session-host.log , in the same folder. It's the one to read when tabs didn't survive: stopping everything : vyberun asked it to stop all tabs (Stop everything, or the Closing vyberun setting). connected, 0 kept right after a start: no tabs were running, for example after Windows restarted. connected, 4 kept : vyberun found 4 tabs still running and brought them back.

head: When vyberun crashed
text: If vyberun closed by itself, Windows records it too: open Event Viewer ▸ Windows Logs ▸ Application and look for an Application Error for vyberun.exe at that time. Its details, together with the last lines of vyberun.log , are what's needed to fix it. See Reporting a problem .
Found a bug, or something in this manual that's wrong? Here's how to report it.

head: Reporting a bug
text: Check that you have the latest version: Help ▸ About vyberun , and the Releases page . Open a new issue on vyberun's issues page . A free GitHub account is needed. Say what you did, what you expected, and what happened instead.

head: What to include
text: vyberun's version, and whether it's the Store version or the zip. Your Windows version ( Settings ▸ System ▸ About ). The lines of vyberun.log from around the time it happened (see Logs ). A screenshot, if it shows the problem. Warning. Before you share a log or a screenshot, read it through. Remove server names, addresses, folder names and anything else you don't want public. Never include a password or a key.

head: Security problems
text: Don't report a security problem in a public issue. Report it privately instead: open vyberun-releases on GitHub , go to its Security tab and choose Report a vulnerability .

head: Mistakes in this manual
text: Report a mistake , at the bottom of every page, opens the same issues page. Say which page, and what's wrong.
